One of them: they are the Prophets.

His Exalted saying: ﴿except for the saying of Ibrahim to his father﴾. The exegetes said: the meaning is, "Take Ibrahim as an example in everything except his asking forgiveness for his father, so do not take him as an example in that, for it was out of a promise he had made to him." ﴿And I cannot avail you anything against Allah.﴾ That is: I cannot ward off from you the punishment of Allah if you associate partners with Him. Among the supplications of Ibrahim and his companions was: ﴿Our Lord, upon You we have relied﴾ up to His saying: ﴿the Mighty, the Wise﴾. Al-Farra' said: You (plural) say, "Our Lord, upon You we have relied." We have already explained the meaning of His saying: ﴿Do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve﴾ in [Yunus] [verse 85].

Then the discourse returned to the mention of the exemplary model, and He said: ﴿There has already been for you a good example in them﴾. That is, in Ibrahim and those with him, because they used to hate whoever opposed Allah. His saying: ﴿for those who hope for Allah﴾ is a substitute for His saying: ﴿for you﴾, and a clarification that this exemplary model is for those who fear Allah and dread the punishment of the Hereafter.

When Allah commanded the believers to be hostile to the disbelievers, they became hostile to their relatives. So Allah revealed: ﴿Perhaps Allah will bring about affection between you and those whom you have made enemies of among them﴾, that is, among the disbelievers of Makkah, "affection." They wrote this document and sealed it. Then Subay'a bint al-Harith al-Aslamiyya came after the document had been completed, while the Prophet was at al-Hudaybiyyah. Her husband came, and he was a disbeliever, and said: 'O Muhammad, return my wife to me, for you have stipulated for us that you would return to us whoever comes to you from us, and this is the clay seal of the document, which has not yet dried.' A group of scholars, among them Muhammad ibn Sa'd, the scribe of al-Waqidi, mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning "Umm Kulthum bint 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'it (p-239), who was the first woman to emigrate to Madinah after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had emigrated. She arrived in Madinah during the truce of al-Hudaybiyyah, and her two brothers, al-Walid and 'Umara, the sons of 'Uqba, set out after her and said: 'O Muhammad, fulfil for us our condition.' Umm Kulthum said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I am a woman, and the state of women in weakness is what you know. Will you return me to the disbelievers, who will tempt me away from my religion, and I have no patience?' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, annulled the covenant concerning women, revealed the test (mihna) regarding them, and judged concerning them with a ruling that all of them accepted. And concerning Umm Kulthum the words ﴿then examine them﴾ were revealed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ examined her, and after her he examined the women, saying: 'By Allah, nothing has brought you out except love of Allah and His Messenger, and you did not leave for a husband or for wealth.' When they said this, they were left alone and were not returned to their families."

The scholars differed about the woman who was the cause of the revelation of this verse, in three opinions.

The first: she is Subay'a, which we have mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: she is Umm Kulthum bint 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'it, which we have mentioned from a group of the people of knowledge, and this is the well-known view.

The third: she is Umayma bint Bishr from the Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, mentioned by Abu Nu'aym al-Isfahani.

Another group said: Their return was not stipulated explicitly in the agreement; rather, the agreement was stated in general terms, and the apparent generality included them along with the men. The first: they are women whose private parts make them forbidden to those men.

The second: they are more tender of heart and quicker to change than men.

As for a woman who remains upon her polytheism, she is returned to them. Al-Qadi Abu Ya'la said: The women were not returned to them because abrogation is permissible after the possibility of acting upon the ruling, even if the act itself did not take place.

Concerning what he examined them with, there are three opinions (p-241).

The first: he examined them with "the testimony that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger." This was related by al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: he would make the woman swear by Allah that she did not leave out of hatred for a husband, nor out of aversion to one land in favour of another, nor in search of worldly gain, and that she left only out of love for Allah and His Messenger. This was also related from Ibn 'Abbas.

The third: he examined them with the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿When believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you﴾. Whoever acknowledged this condition would say: "I have pledged allegiance to you." This is the view of 'A'isha.

Then it is not lawful to return them "to the disbelievers" ["for Allah the Exalted has not permitted a believing woman to a polytheist"; "and give them" meaning their disbelieving husbands] ﴿what they have spent﴾, meaning the dowry (mahr). If no one marries her, then her disbelieving husband has no claim to anything. ﴿And there is no blame upon you if you marry them when you have given them their bridal payments﴾, which are the dowries (p-242).

According to us, if a free woman emigrates after her husband has consummated the marriage with her, the separation takes effect upon the end of her waiting period ('idda). If the husband embraces Islam before the end of her waiting period, she remains his wife. This is the view of al-Awza'i, al-Layth, Malik and al-Shafi'i. Abu Hanifa said: separation takes effect with the difference of the two abodes.

Allah's words: ﴿And do not hold on to disbelieving women in marriage﴾. Ibn Kathir, Nafi', 'Asim, Ibn 'Amir, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read (tumsikū) with a dammah on the ta' and without doubling the sin. Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub read (tumassikū) with a dammah on the ta' and with doubling of the sin. Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrima, al-Hasan, Ibn Ya'mar and Abu Haywa read (tamassakū) with a fatha on the ta' and the mim, and the sin doubled. "Al-kawafir" is the plural of kafira (disbelieving woman). The meaning is that Allah the Exalted forbade the believers from remaining in marriage with disbelieving women, and commanded them to separate from them. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that when she disbelieves, the bond ( 'isma) between her and the believer is gone, that is, the marriage contract has been severed.

The root of 'isma is a rope, and whatever holds something is called its 'isma.

Allah's words: ﴿And ask for what you have spent﴾, meaning: if a woman from among you joins the disbelievers who have a covenant (ahl al-'ahd) as an apostate, then ask them for what you have spent of the dowry if they do not hand her over to you. ﴿And let them ask for what they have spent﴾, meaning the polytheists whose wives joined you as believers, when they marry among you; so their disbelieving husbands should ask whoever married them for ﴿what they have spent﴾, which is the dowry. The meaning is: you are obliged to pay them the dowry as they would pay you.

The people of the biographies (ahl al-siyar) said: When Umm Kulthum emigrated, she was an unmarried young woman with no husband to whom the amount of her dowry could be sent. When she emigrated, she married Zayd ibn Haritha.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 60, verse 12:

The words of God Most High: ﴿When believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you﴾. The exegetes said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) conquered Makkah, women came to him to pledge allegiance, so this verse was revealed. He set for their pledge the conditions mentioned in the verse, and he accepted their pledge while he was at al-Safa. When he said, "and they shall not commit adultery," Hind said, "Does a free woman commit adultery?" He said, "and they shall not kill their children," and she said, "We raised them when they were small, and you killed them when they were grown; so you and they know best." It is established in a hadith that "the Prophet (ﷺ) did not shake hands with any woman in the pledge of allegiance; he only pledged them with words." We have named, as far as we have counted, those women who pledged allegiance, in the book "al-Talqih," in alphabetical order of the letters; they number four hundred and fifty-seven women. And God is the Granter of success.

The words of God Most High: ﴿and they shall not kill their children﴾. The exegetes said: this is the burying alive (al-wa'd) that the Jahiliyyah used to practise.

The words of God Most High: ﴿and they shall not bring a slander that they have invented between their hands and their feet﴾. Concerning this there are three opinions.

The first: they shall not attribute to their husbands children other than their own. This was said by Ibn Abbas and the majority. The reason is that a woman would pick up a newborn and say to her husband, "This is my child from you," and that is the invented slander. He said "between their hands and their feet" because when the mother gives birth, the child falls between her hands and her feet. It was also said that the meaning of "they invent it between their hands" is that they take in a foundling (laqit), and "their feet" refers to what they bore from fornication.

The second: sorcery.

The third: walking about with tale-bearing and striving in corruption. Al-Mawardi mentioned these two.

The words of God Most High: ﴿and they shall not disobey you in what is right﴾. Concerning this there are three opinions.

(p-٢٤٧) The first: it is wailing, said by Ibn Abbas, and it has been transmitted as a marfu' report from the Prophet (ﷺ).

The second: that they shall not call out "woe," nor scratch the face, nor loosen the hair, nor tear garments; this was said by Zayd ibn Aslam.

The third: all that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) commands them of the laws and etiquette of Islam; this was said by Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi. In this verse is evidence that obedience to rulers is binding only in what is permissible, not in what is forbidden.

The words of God Most High: ﴿so accept their pledge﴾. The meaning: when they pledge to you upon these conditions, then accept their pledge.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 60, verse 13:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, do not make allies of a people with whom Allah has been angry﴾ — meaning the Jews. This is because some of the poor Muslims used to inform the Jews of the news of the Muslims, seeking nearness to them by this, so that they might obtain some of their fruits and food. So this verse was revealed.

(p-248) His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They have despaired of the Hereafter﴾. This is because the Jews, by their denial of Muhammad (ﷺ) while they know his truthfulness, have despaired that there would be any good for them in the Hereafter. The meaning: they have despaired of the reward of the Hereafter. This is the saying of the majority (al-Jumhur), and it is the correct view. Qatadah said: "They have despaired of being resurrected." ﴿As the disbelievers have despaired﴾ — concerning this there are two views.

One of them: "As the disbelievers have despaired of the resurrection of those in the graves." This was said by Ibn Abbas.

The second: "As the disbelievers who have died have despaired of the reward of the Hereafter, because they have become certain of the punishment." This was said by Mujahid.
